events.text: Document Directory SD
1. What Is This Service Domain?

The Document Directory Service Domain in BIAN v13.0 is responsible for recording and exposing document entries — specifically the storage path URLs of documents collected, generated, or uploaded across any banking process.

It acts as the authoritative document registry and reference layer for a given documentdirectoryid (Document Directory Instance Reference). The actual binary files are stored in any compatible external storage system — only the URLs and metadata persisted in this SD.
1.1 Key Distinction

rows: Document metadata and storage location references (URLs)
Store actual document files — binaries live in the external storage system
Authoritative document registry and reference layer across banking processes
documentdirectoryid — Document Directory Instance Reference, unique per registered document

events.text: 2. When to Use This Service Domain

This Service Domain can be invoked across any banking process or journey wherever document metadata and storage location references need to be registered or retrieved. It is not limited to any specific journey.

As part of the current implementation scope, it is being used during the customer onboarding journey. The same SD will be reused as-is whenever other journeys require document registration or retrieval — no changes to the SD will be needed.
2.1 Invocation Scenarios

rows: Once a document is uploaded to a compatible storage system and a storage URL is obtained, invoke Register to persist document metadata and URL for future retrieval and audit.
Retrieve the stored file path from the Document Directory, then use the returned URL to access the document from the storage system. Enables viewing, audit, or downstream processing.

events.text: 2.2 Prerequisite

rows: Documents must be uploaded to any compatible storage system BEFORE invoking the Document Directory endpoints. The APIs for document upload to the storage system are outside the scope of this Service Domain and must be handled separately.

events.text: 3. SD Scope — Level of Details to Capture
This is an Operational Document Registry Service Domain — not a content store. Data captured must be metadata-accurate, location-referenced, and status-aware.

rows: Document Type, Document Identifier Value (e.g. Passport Number)
Creation Date, Capture DateTime, Signing Date, Issue Date, Validity From / Validity To
Authority Name, Authority Type, Party Involvement Type
Storage URL / File Path (DocumentLocation) — mandatory field
Active / Expired / Rejected — drives integration flows

events.text: 4. Behaviour Qualifiers (BQs)
No Behaviour Qualifier endpoints were introduced in this implementation. All operations are at the Control Record (CR) level only.
5. SD Data Model — Document Details to Capture
The following represents the full set of data the SD can hold per Document Directory entry, categorised by data group:

rows: Record-level CR timestamp — when the document was created
Channel upload timestamp — when the document was captured by the channel
Start of bank-validity period for the document
End of bank-validity period for the document
Document name / type — Defaulted to: Business Document
The identifier value of the document e.g. Passport Number
Enum: Document date type e.g. IssueDate
Description of document content e.g. Identity Proof
Purpose of the document e.g. Address Proof
Subject of the document e.g. Customer Address Proof
Customer-provided document description captured through channel
File type e.g. JPG, PNG, PDF — needed for rendering
Name of the issuing authority e.g. US Department of State
Type of issuing authority e.g. Organisation
Storage URL — the link to the document in the external storage system (Mandatory)
Overall document status e.g. Active / Expired — drives integration flows (Mandatory)
Status reason for the media format entry e.g. Verified

events.text: 6. Cross-SD Traceability
The documentdirectoryid returned by POST /DocumentDirectory/Register must be stored in the relevant Service Domain via DocumentDirectoryEntryInstanceReference for cross-SD traceability.

Example: Party Reference Data Directory SD stores this parameter in its CIF DB so it can call GET /DocumentDirectory/{documentdirectoryid}/Retrieve to retrieve any party-related documents when needed.
7. Future Scope — Not in Current Implementation

rows: Tracking multiple versions of the same document
Automated alerts when document validity period ends
Multi-step approval before a document is marked Active
Full audit history of document access and status changes

events.text: 8. BIAN Field Mapping

rows: Business Document, Financial Document, Commercial Document
Jerry Todd Holmes's Passport issued in United States

events.text: 9. BIAN Version Note

rows: The BIAN V14 published API payload for Document Directory is currently insufficient and is a work in progress. The current implementation is based on BIAN V13 temporarily and will be upgraded to V14 once BIAN publishes the complete specification.
